summary: EarthSona is an interactive, accessibility-focused prototype that explores how NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations can be experienced through sound. Our project aims to transform complex environmental information, particularly air-quality and PM2.5 data, into meaningful auditory experiences that help users perceive patterns and changes in Earth's atmosphere. By connecting visual environmental information with sonification, EarthSona seeks to make scientific data more engaging, understandable, and accessible, especially for people who are blind or have low vision. The prototype's interface demonstrates the intended user experience, while our research investigates NASA's GEOS-CF atmospheric datasets and establishes a scientific foundation for future data integration. EarthSona handles the challenge by exploring an alternative way to experience Earth science: not only seeing changes in our planet, but also hearing them. Its broader goal is to make NASA's environmental information more inclusive and encourage new ways of communicating scientific discoveries.
details:
Details — EarthSona

EarthSona is an accessibility-focused interactive prototype designed to make NASA Earth science information understandable through sound. It explores how environmental visualizations, particularly air-quality information, can be translated into auditory experiences so that users can not only see changes in Earth's atmosphere but also hear them.

How It Works

EarthSona is designed around a connection between NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations and sonification. Its intended workflow involves processing environmental information, extracting meaningful patterns such as changes in PM2.5 concentrations, and translating those patterns into sound through carefully designed audio mappings. Users are intended to explore the information through synchronized visual and auditory experiences.

Our team developed an initial interface prototype using simulated sample values for design demonstration. Separately, we investigated NASA GEOS-CF atmospheric datasets, examining PM2.5 variables, timestamps, spatial resolution, data quality, and limitations. This research provides a scientific foundation for integrating authentic NASA data into the application.

Benefits and Intended Impact

EarthSona aims to:

  • Improve access to environmental information for people who are blind or have low vision.
  • Provide an alternative way to understand complex atmospheric patterns.
  • Make NASA scientific visualizations more interactive and engaging.
  • Encourage curiosity about air quality, atmospheric processes, and environmental science.
  • Demonstrate how accessibility can be incorporated into scientific data communication.

Its intended impact is to make Earth science more inclusive by allowing environmental information to be experienced through multiple senses.

Tools and Technologies

Our development approach combines scientific data analysis and interactive web development. The research and data-inspection work used Python, NumPy, Pandas, xarray, NetCDF4, and Matplotlib to investigate NASA GEOS-CF files. The planned application architecture uses React, TypeScript, and Vite for the interface, with Tone.js and Web Audio technologies for sound generation. Python and FastAPI are intended to support data processing and integration.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of EarthSona is its approach to scientific communication: transforming environmental information into an auditory experience rather than presenting it exclusively through maps, charts, and animations. Instead of treating sound as background decoration, the project aims to make it an informative representation of environmental data.

Factors Considered

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability, data reliability, and the relationship between visual and auditory information. We also investigated the limitations of model-generated atmospheric data and the importance of distinguishing simulated interface samples from authentic NASA data. Our design prioritizes meaningful sound mappings, clear explanations, and the possibility of future expansion to other environmental variables.
